title: HB1222 (114th General Assembly): AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 36 and Title 39, relative to emergency protection orders.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Tennessee); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Tennessee text (Draft, 2025-02-06; official copy via LegiScan getBillText doc 3105174)
provenance.note: Draft as introduced (2025-02-06); no amendments in text read. Twin SB 1131 is on the same document. Standard of proof for the final order is preponderance of the evidence; orders last up to one year, renewable. Quote of 39-17-1904(a) and 39-17-1905(f) joins numbered subdivisions in order.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1901(a)): A family member, household member, intimate partner, or law enforcement officer who has a reasonable belief that a person poses an imminent risk of harm to the person or others if allowed to purchase or possess a firearm may seek relief under this part by filing a sworn petition for an emergency protection order against the respondent.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1902(a)): An ex parte emergency protection order must prohibit the respondent from purchasing or possessing any firearm during the period that the order is in effect.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1904(a)): (1) It is an offense to knowingly violate an emergency protection order. (2) A violation of subdivision (a)(1) is a Class A misdemeanor.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1905(b)(1)): To terminate the respondent's physical possession of the firearms in the respondent's possession by any lawful means, such as transferring possession to a third party who is not prohibited from possessing firearms, within forty-eight (48) hours; and
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1905(f)): (1) It is an offense for a person subject to an emergency protection order to knowingly fail to surrender or transfer all firearms the respondent possesses as required by this section. (2) A violation of subdivision (f)(1) is a Class A misdemeanor, and each violation constitutes a separate offense.
